items.analysis: Murray has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain and is considered week-to-week, paving the way for Carson Wentz to make his second start of the season when the Vikings face the Bills on MNF. Per Lewis, head coach Kevin O'Connell said Thursday that a stint on injured reserve isn't under consideration for Murray, suggesting that the starting quarterback's absence isn't expected to linger beyond 1-3 weeks.
items.headline: Out Monday due to hamstring strain, won't go on IR
items.notes: Murray (hamstring) won't play Monday against the Bills, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.

items.analysis: Wentz will get the Week 9 assignment at QB for the Vikings, with Kyler Murray viewed as week-to-week with a hamstring strain, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Max Brosmer will be the team's backup versus Buffalo, and perhaps longer should Murray's injury linger. Wentz  thus represents an option for those in Superflex formats or are otherwise in need of signal-caller help due to injury or bye week issues.
items.headline: In line to draw MNF start
items.notes: Wentz is stated to start Monday night's game against the Bills, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.

items.analysis: With Watson, who is in the NFL's concussion protocol, in line to log back-to-back 'DNPs," the QB's status for Sunday's game against the Saints remains cloudy. In the event that Watson doesn't gain clearance to play this weekend, Shedeur Sanders would draw the start in his place.
items.headline: Missing another practice
items.notes: Watson (concussion) remained sidelined from practice Thursday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.

items.analysis: Watson was listed as a limited participant at Wednesday's practice after sustaining a rib injury in Green Bay's Week 8 win over the Panthers. His participation level Thursday has yet to be revealed, but it's a good sign that Watson is able to practice in pads and take contact as the Packers prepare to face the Patriots on Sunday.
items.headline: Practicing in pads Thursday
items.notes: Watson (ribs) is wearing pads for Thursday's practice, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.

items.analysis: Wilson also logged a 'DNP' on Wednesday, so the wideout's apparent absence from Wednesday's session sets the stage for Friday's practice to loom large in terms of his availability for Sunday's game against the Chiefs. In the event that Wilson isn't cleared to play, added targets would be available for some combo of WRs Omar Cooper, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams, as well as tight ends Mason Taylor (back) and Kenyon Sadiq.
items.headline: Not spotted at practice Thursday
items.notes: Wilson, who is in the NFL's concussion protocol, wasn't seen at Thursday's practice, , Antwan Staley of the New York Daily News reports.

items.analysis: Hall, who was a limited participant at Wednesday's practice session, was also limited throughout the week leading up to the Jets' Week 8 loss to the Raiders, which the running back sat out. While the team's coaching staff has expressed optimism that Hall will be ready to return Sunday against the Chiefs, his status will remain up in the air until he's able to practice without limitations. Thursday's participation level has yet to be revealed, but Hall's presence at practice suggests that he has at least avoided a setback.
items.headline: Practicing again Thursday
items.notes: Hall (quadriceps) is participating in Thursday's practice, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.

items.analysis: Karty was elevated from the practice squad for each of the Rams' previous two games and handled kickoff duties while Brandon McManus kicked field goals and extra points. That arrangement isn't expected to change moving forward, per Nate Adkins of The Athletic, so it would likely take a McManus slump or injury for Karty to get a shot at the fantasy-relevant aspects of the kicker position.
items.headline: Joins McManus on active roster
items.notes: The Rams signed Karty to their active roster Thursday.

items.analysis: Rodriguez fell three tackles shy of Jordyn Brooks' team-leading total as the Dolphins dropped to 1-6. The rookie second-round pick's 12 tackles over the past two games mark the most fallow two-game stretch of Rodriguez's young career in that category. He'll try to pick up the pace in Week 9 against the Lions.
items.headline: Eight tackles in Week 8
items.notes: Rodriguez notched eight tackles (two solo) and forced a fumble in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots.

items.analysis: Brooks led the Dolphins in tackles during the loss, which dropped Miami's record to 1-6. The 29-year-old linebacker has slowed down a bit after leading the NFL with 183 tackles (99 solo) during the 2025 regular season, though he's still averaging a respectable nine tackles per game in 2026. He could draw interest on the trade market from contending teams in search of help at linebacker.
items.headline: Notches 11 tackles in Week 8
items.notes: Brooks recorded 11 tackles (six solo) in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots.
